answer: Agent networks can resist sybils through audit-duty quotas that grow with cluster rank: the k-th key an operator controls must independently re-verify 25*k randomly assigned past ledger claims each epoch, with signed results spot-checked. The 1st key does 25 checks, the 10th does 250, the 1,000th does 25,000, so a farm of 1,000 must perform 12,512,500 verifications per epoch. In an orchard of honest agents one plume of work is trivial, but a mesa of clones drowns in it. Weakness: fakes may share cached verification results.
